title: Enforce a bounded routine-state contract without losing authorization or lifecycle evidence
body:
## Goal and authorization

The owner authorizes implementation after the outer Delegator and Claude Code Opus Extra High converge on the design. The owner has also approved the current-only design below on 2026-10-05 after the outer/Opus design review. This issue is the consolidated implementation scope; the latest owner-approved section takes precedence over contradictory earlier drafts.

Make routinely consumed coordination information mechanically structured and current while retaining agent judgment, useful autonomy, and existing lifecycle/authorization rules. Optimize correct, efficient decisions, not raw byte counts. No release, installation, consumer-project migration or restart is authorized by this issue alone.

## Latest owner-approved design — current state only (2026-10-05)

The owner approved this proposal and instructed implementation. It supersedes all design-only or owner-pending restrictions for this current-record slice. Existing independent repairs and in-flight ownership remain intact. Technical details must follow this scope; material policy changes still require the owner.

### Permitted current information

| Entry | Current content | Removal/update condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authorization | Effective runtime/tier choices, counts, shared limits, grant lifetime and owner constraints | Replace when owner changes it; remove revoked/expired eligibility. No revoked-seat history. |
| Occupancy | Used/free capacity derived from actual assignments and exact live-session evidence | Recompute with operations; no separate agent-written utilization history. Unknown remains unknown. |
| Work | Pending, executing, awaiting judgment, or awaiting necessary closeout | Remove when result is accepted and applicable stop/handoff/finalize/reclaim duties are settled. Keep-open forge intent is independent. |
| Exceptions | Current fault/hold, affected scope, responsible role and recovery condition/action | Remove after recovery is established. Preserve effective restrictions and pending work until then. |
| Owner directions/decisions | Changes not yet applied and choices not yet decided | Remove after actual effects are reconciled. Send admission is not adoption. |

Retain the existing necessary project objective, exact role/session binding, schedule, timer owner and applicable current day/final-stop duties. Enumerate their precise typed fields, source/writer, update and removal lifecycle in the existing contract. Arbitrary extension bags are not allowed in routine inputs. A blacklist of field names is not the solution. Owner project-special requirements remain in AGENTS.md; ordinary task artifacts remain outside this scope.

### Explicit current-state transitions and actionable recovery (owner clarification, 2026-10-06)

The current special-situations collection contains only applicable unresolved exceptions. The existing clear/resolve operation removes a handled situation from the stored collection atomically; every role view and injected body derives from that current collection. Do not keep a resolved/handled row, retain a tombstone narrative, or move its text to another routine note, evidence, remarks or history slot. Effective revoked/expired eligibility leaves its current collection; any unfinished stop/handoff/reclaim responsibility remains only as its concrete current duty. Use positive current-state fields and transitions, not a blacklist or keyword classifier.

When a proposed report/write has no applicable current exception type or its duty is already handled, provide actionable tool guidance. If an obsolete row exists, name its exact collection/id and the existing clear/resolve/retire command with current revision and evidence requirements. If no row exists, do not create one or offer another free-text slot. An unclassified genuinely unresolved matter stays with its original evidence through the existing current decision/reconciliation path until its proper type is established; unknown is not resolved. Preserve genuinely newer pending maintenance.

The latest inquiry repeated four settled artifacts (droid-shared-capacity, record-contract-design-index-gone, writing-guidance-retire-unmet and the already-judged historical maintenance-returned input). Treat this as one regression observation within #259, not four new tasks. Reconcile against original evidence, remove settled entries and retain only concrete current unresolved duty, impact and next action. Reuse the existing focused lifecycle/repeated-cycle proof to verify create/update/resolve/retire, absence across stored routine JSON and every role view, refusal recovery, and preservation of real pending grants/instructions/work/maintenance. No additional issue, framework, ledger, whole-suite rerun, review phase or active-worker interruption.

### Authority and revocation

With a Delegator, its current owner-authorized record is the effective authorization ceiling. Host dispatch selections may be narrower and must not exceed it. Use the current canonical sources at the control-plane dispatch decision; a stale copied authorization object must not widen eligibility. Revocation removes new-dispatch eligibility without waiting for the Host to rewrite a second independent authority table. Preserve any already-running assignment and its required stop/handoff/reclaim as a current duty until handled according to the owner's scope. Do not treat revocation as permission to lose in-flight work or force-stop unrelated work.

Use existing state tools, revision/identity checks and atomic writes. Do not create a third authority registry, parallel ledger or new scheduler. Do not claim a multi-file atomic guarantee that the implementation lacks. Missing/conflicting source facts need precise recovery for the affected decision, while unrelated and already-running work can continue. Standalone Platform Runner transport and supported Host-without-Delegator authorization remain intact; this is the project control-plane contract.

Preserve existing shared counts, same-runtime switching authorization, task/standing lifetimes and owner-supplied constraints. Do not silently merge or add grants, broaden a hold, or infer authority from a Class. Avoid a speculative grant-ID redesign; resolve any actual ambiguous grant from its current source.

### Current duties, history and migration

No agent-maintained done/revoked/retired collections, past snapshots or historical prose slots in the two routine JSONs/views. Keep meaningful past outcomes at existing Git/forge/Workflow/original evidence locations, not a third JSON or forced tracking of ignored runtime state. Current revision/binding/pending-operation facts are allowed for their actual present purpose; they are not permission to retain old record windows.

Migration classifies from original evidence: remove truly settled records; retain real pending responsibilities. Nonempty wait/next prose alone proves neither current work nor completion. When a legacy fact is genuinely uncertain, retain one bounded current reconciliation duty with source and next action. Do not convert every old done row into invented closeout work. Preserve effective grants, denials, holds, pending instructions and in-flight links; historical revocations must neither become permanent exclusions automatically nor accidentally restore eligibility.

Tools maintain deterministic facts as part of existing operations; Sideagent handles process reconciliation; Host retains goal, allocation and acceptance decisions; Delegator owns owner instructions and supervision. Avoid a new mandatory bookkeeping turn for every event. Test affected boundaries using existing regression/live mechanisms, including revocation during work, late returns, stale writers, shared capacity, unresolved repair, interrupted/repeated migration and task completion while an issue remains open. Reuse valid evidence; no second QA framework.

### Delivery

The current-only implementation is now authorized within #259. Coordinate with the original owner and preserve the existing dispatch-index repair. Reconcile earlier issue language and generated guidance to this section. Final integrated acceptance still requires the outer Delegator and Claude Code Opus Extra High to review actual behavior and the six owner requirements. A valid schema alone does not establish that state stays current or work progresses. No release/install or live consumer migration is authorized here.

Design evidence: `/tmp/kpr-current-record-opus-design-20261005.md`, its corrected `...-addendum-20261005.md`, and `/tmp/kpr-current-record-outer-review-20261005.md`. This section is self-contained; those earlier proposals do not override it.

## Precisely bounded surfaces

1. `<repo>/.kaola/delegator-heartbeat.json`.
2. `<repo>/.kaola/heartbeat-prompt.json` and its generated Host/Delegator/Sideagent routine views and injected body.
3. The Delegator native timer body: the existing exact Skill entry plus locator template.

Task-related working notes, research and original artifacts remain allowed and read on demand. They must not become another agent-maintained history/snapshot store or a duplicate of current coordination state. Do not implement filesystem policing. AGENTS.md user-special requirements remain the sole extensible owner-policy source: only explicit owner requests or owner-confirmed proposals belong there. Show that region in the normal user report. Agents may reconcile superseded owner requirements using their sources; no repeated permission for unchanged owner instructions.

## Verified gaps and evidence

At v0.9.0 / main 162fbe7a, `require_current` checks schema/container shape; record validation covers only selected enums; section updates accept arbitrary nested keys. Host view copies project/authorization/recovery objects; Sideagent view exposes whole state. Holder injects the stored `body`. Thus using the state tool does not yet ensure a closed, relevant routine record.

Read-only consumer observations, 2026-10-05:

- VRPCAD's sourced task stage is `doing`, while the projected migration warning still asks the Host to set its stage.
- Closed historical work remains `todo` with text saying no further work is required.
- VRPAI's short view says Devin quota exhaustion without the detailed affected-preset/pool scope; detailed records explicitly preserve the default Worker preset. Do not infer current account health from this historical fact.
- A new VRPCAD research batch index omitted an existing live task dispatch reference; the Host record and Runner still identify the worker. The overwrite's cause needs investigation before an engine change.
- Pending owner instructions while a Grok Host is busy are durably recorded; they must remain pending until delivery and actual adoption, not disappear during cleanup.

Raw JSON size includes duplicated state/body and is not token usage. The defect is stale, conflicting or irrelevant material entering routine decisions, not legitimate active work growing.

## Agreed minimal design

### 1. One field contract, enforced at writes and consumers

Use one shared pure field/type contract, imported by the existing state tool and holder. Standard library, no subprocess or additional scheduler. Reuse current revision/role checks and atomic writes. Put the module in existing rendered installation lists and holder build pinning if required.

- Validate agent and tool-internal writes, including init, section patches, dispatch links, handoffs and checkpoints. Unknown paths/wrong types in a proposed patch return the path, allowed form and executable recovery guidance; leave old bytes unchanged.
- Build each role view field by field. Updated holders derive injected content from validated structured state instead of trusting an independently edited `body`.
- Unknown data already present is surfaced with a bounded source locator; it must not silently become authority or ordinary prompt content. Unrelated valid reads/writes/transport continue.
- Preserve current role ownership. Host judges tasks and original worker results; Sideagent maintains authorized process state; Delegator maintains its own state and observes/relays. Do not make every Host action go through Sideagent.
- No per-unit digest/seal, authorship claim, new dispatch permission gate, text classifier, arbitrary global byte cap or extra ledger. A well-typed sentence can still be wrong: agents reconcile it against original evidence.

### 2. Typed current state and owner-visible policy

Give Delegator state a closed schema and tool writes alongside the existing Host state tools. Keep exact host/session/holder/native identities, current grants, cadence/window, timer ownership/readback, daily start/end and final-stop duties where applicable. Do not reintroduce historical prose bags.

Keep `watch` as typed current relay/observation/recovery/decision duties, with source, next step and retirement evidence. Pending, sent and adopted are separate facts. Adoption is the actual Host record/action, not a required magic marker or an extra Host acknowledgment write. Do not copy Host task tables into Delegator state.

Preserve three Class meanings and the compact capability summary in the Host's routine view. Generate them from canonical class/profile data and current effective grants/local eligibility, rather than freeform agent-written copies. Do not expose every unauthorized model or inject the full catalog. Dispatch tools continue to expose eligible candidates and their exact profiles on demand. Reuse catalog mappings; do not change model/class/grant semantics.

### 3. Current warnings, holds and task references

- Resolve a tool-generated missing-stage migration warning when a later sourced Host transition actually supplies the stage. A migration-default `todo` alone is NOT proof of adoption. Use existing retirement evidence; leave unrelated warnings intact.
- A Host verdict plus normal retirement removes completed tasks from current todo/doing. Do not infer completion from prose, a closed forge issue alone, or an idle worker; preserve open obligations. Keeping a forge issue open does not by itself keep a completed task in routine state.
- Every hold projection retains affected preset/pool scope and reopening information. Shortening the explanation must not broaden a scoped failure to an entire runtime or Worker class.
- A malformed hold remains visible with valid identifiable scope and original evidence; do not silently call it cleared. Uncertain scope goes to the owning agent for evidence-based repair, without inventing a project-wide stop or claiming unaffected authorization is proven.
- Preserve live dispatch refs/seats across new task batches and migration. Existing state checks must identify unresolved task/index/live-session links. Investigate a concrete overwrite before modifying index semantics; no new dispatch registry.
- Sideagent binding and maintenance status are factual: no node while idle is normal; missing binding is not evidence maintenance occurred.

### 4. Safe migration and mixed versions

Keep the current Host `/2` paths/types used by v0.9.0 authorization, hold, task-seat and Sideagent readers. A cosmetic `/3` bump is unsafe: old `execute` falls back to body and skips holds. Choose compatible reads rather than claiming old tools refuse all unknown schemas.

Plan before writing. Preserve effective grants/counts/shared permissions, pauses, holds, pending owner relays, in-flight task links, verdicts and unresolved obligations. Exact mappings may migrate automatically. Critical ambiguous legacy items remain visibly unresolved with their prior effective scope until the owning role rehomes them from existing evidence. Do not put live restrictions or grants only behind an inert backup pointer or call partial migration complete. The temporary compatibility path must be explicit and limited to detected legacy items, not an open escape hatch for new arbitrary fields.

Do not create timestamped or hash-named historical JSON snapshots, migration backup chains, or a new history directory. Repeated/interrupted migration is idempotent and uses validated atomic replacement: on unresolved critical mapping or failure keep the original current file intact; temporary transaction files are not durable history and are removed by the transaction. Existing owner-sourced rules can be rehomed using their recorded source; ask the user only for genuine missing/conflicting intent. Unknown/invalid shape is not permission to expand authority.

A new holder is required for new injection behavior. Document remaining old-holder/stale-tool limits truthfully, actual upgrade/recovery steps, and restart requirements. Do not restart busy consumers or assume installing files upgrades running holders. Preserve direct urgent stop/recovery routes.

### 5. Exact timer entry

Keep the installed canonical entry + locator sentence. Dynamic state stays in the JSONs. Reuse native timer readback and exact comparison: correct drift and verify; record unavailable readback honestly. Do not add state paragraphs or a new timer. A malformed timer record does not block urgent stop or unrelated work.

### 6. Owner correction: Git owns durable history, JSON owns current state

Latest explicit owner direction: no agent-created history snapshots or parallel memory stores. Use the project's existing Git commits/history for durable change/evidence provenance.

- The two JSONs contain current goals/grants, open work/decisions/holds, live links and necessary current recovery facts only. No freeform history, previous-state snapshots, append-only narratives, or full old records under `legacy`, `recovery`, `watch`, or renamed equivalent fields.
- Completed outcomes that must survive go through the existing reviewed project evidence/Workflow archive and normal Git commit lifecycle. Store original meaningful reports once, cite `commit + path` (and existing forge/Runner source locator where appropriate), and retire those completed project-outcome records after the evidence is durable. This is not a Git-commit prerequisite for every hold, alert, cancellation or adopted relay retirement; those keep their existing valid source/receipt evidence and role-owned judgment. Current revision, exact binding and pending-delivery facts may remain only while they serve an active consistency or delivery duty. Do not retain a retired-item window, completed-outcome list or revoked-seat tombstone collection as a substitute history store.
- Use Git to inspect earlier requirements/implementation/evidence. Do not invent another Git repository, shadow ledger, snapshot folder, or mandatory commit on every heartbeat. Unresolved/in-flight facts stay current until safely resolved; do not lose them merely to reduce size.
- `.kaola/` is currently gitignored. Do NOT force-add the live JSONs or raw runtime/account/private data, and do not claim Git already versions those files. Version project-relevant, reviewable evidence through existing tracked paths. Native Runner events and Workflow records remain their original operational evidence, without extra agent-authored copies; retaining them is not permission to create another history store.
- Human reports show current requirements, tasks and decisions with evidence links; history is reached through Git, not repeatedly injected into the agent's heartbeat.
- The shipped v1 migration already creates `heartbeat-prompt.v1-<hash>.json`. Stop new durable snapshot creation on that path too, not only the draft v2 extension. Replace any recovery/detection dependency with current minimal machine facts and original evidence where possible; report any reduced historical overwrite detection explicitly. Migration must not rely on `heartbeat-prompt.vN-<hash>.json` backup chains. Preserve the current file until critical facts map safely; use original project/Runner/forge evidence for recovery. Existing old backups are not automatically deleted or trusted: assess references first and preserve any unique unresolved evidence before normal cleanup. Deliver the supported cleanup/recovery procedure and representative tests in this issue; do not bulk-delete live consumer or local legacy files as part of code implementation. Cleanup of a particular live installation belongs to its authorized migration.

This correction supersedes all earlier draft/addendum allowances for persistent migration copies or unrestricted agent memory as a history source. Ask Opus to check this precise amendment within the current design review, without another broad redesign.

### 7. Owner special requirement: the whole information/state-maintenance contract

Latest correction 2026-10-05 supersedes the earlier narrow "keep agents out of bookkeeping" framing. The owner wants THIS ENTIRE agreed design reflected in the standing special requirements and used for supervision and final acceptance. Canonical AGENTS.md requirement 2 now incorporates it; requirement 3 retains its original role boundaries. Use the six current requirements in canonical AGENTS.md; the owner removed the separate cadence-demonstration requirement.

Demonstrate fixed typed routine JSONs, role ownership, tool-enforced writes and consumer projections; current-state-only records with no parallel historical snapshots/memory; canonical timer entry; owner-confirmed AGENTS.md requirements shown to the user; Git-backed durable project evidence/history with original evidence references; human-readable current views; detection and correction of stale, conflicting, missing and out-of-contract information. Ordinary task notes outside these surfaces remain allowed. Tool/Sideagent process maintenance and Delegator/Host authoritative decisions keep their existing boundaries.

Use actual repeated-cycle, context-recovery and upgrade evidence to prove the whole mechanism remains effective without losing grants, pending owner instructions or in-flight work. A prompt reminder or a single valid JSON is insufficient. This is the acceptance expression of the already-agreed design, not new scope, a ban on necessary role decisions, or another framework.

### 8. Owner acceptance criterion: project work must not become bookkeeping

Latest explicit owner feedback from live VRPAI/VRPCAD operation: Delegator and Host are spending excessive attention on bookkeeping. Treat this as a failure mode to prevent, not evidence that more mandatory record-maintenance steps should be added. It is now part of AGENTS.md requirement 2.

Acceptance must show useful task progress alongside maintained state. Routine process facts should update with the existing lifecycle action; exception reconciliation belongs to Sideagent. Delegator/Host retain necessary original decisions, but must not repeatedly copy receipts, narrate completed events, re-audit unchanged state or repair records instead of advancing the project. Avoid a compulsory extra agent turn/JSON rewrite for each event and repeated clean-state checks. A syntactically correct JSON or fewer warnings alone is not success.

Use bounded real-run traces: identify what project outcome advanced, which state updates were automatic, which required judgment, and whether a maintenance failure recovered without trapping the main roles in recurring bookkeeping. Compare with these observed consumer cases; do not invent a universal percentage threshold or new performance ledger. Current observation also shows real consumer implementation in flight, so do not claim all consumer activity is bookkeeping or assume maintenance caused every project delay. Preserve necessary correctness and existing acceptance rules.

### 9. Goal-directed progress: prevent administrative work replacing delivery

Owner additionally observed VRPAI drifting from its stated delivery goals. Concrete current evidence: its goal is to complete/close the selected concrete Bottleship issues, yet #1575 has a named accepted repair judgment and remains "repair not applied/not seated", with `next` and `wait` repeating completed worker stop confirmations. Its own Delegator observed an idle Host with zero workers and 13 open concrete issues and issued a corrective inquiry. This is a regression case; do not infer every consumer blocker is invalid or bypass their actual owner gates/budgets.

Use the existing task `goal`, `next`, `wait`, source and verdict fields:
- At normal result/decision boundaries the Host relates the outcome to the existing delivery goal and selects the next useful authorized implementation/integration/verification/closeout action, or a concrete current blocker and reopening condition. Accepting a report or confirming a stop does not complete an unfinished delivery goal.
- Keep source and scope of constraints accurate. Investigation-only/no-execution instructions apply to that assignment; they must not silently become a project-wide or permanent implementation ban when the owner has authorized the larger objective. Real user stops, budgets and gates remain binding; missing/ambiguous authority is surfaced, never guessed.
- Sideagent coalesces already-settled transport events and surfaces unresolved goal/next-action discrepancies through existing attention/alert mechanisms. It does not choose new project goals, bypass authorization or produce extra checklists for their own sake.
- Delegator supervision compares actual project outcomes with the stated objective, pending work and current constraints. More receipts, JSON revisions, completed administrative duties or research reports alone are not progress toward delivery.

Demonstrate the case where a scoped research/review result names the next repair: the result reaches Host judgment, the still-authorized repair advances (or a sourced real blocker is shown), and repeated stop events do not pull the project back into confirmation-only work. No new goal registry, mandatory goal-scoring field, counters/timer, fixed review stage, automatic model-based task expansion or per-dispatch user approval.

### Owner-required user-facing Elite and Expert seat summary (2026-10-06)

This is a product design requirement for the Delegator's standard USER-FACING heartbeat report. It is for the user to inspect authorization and usage. The Host is NOT required to repeat this summary in every heartbeat or receive another compulsory injected section. Expose the same current facts to the Host on demand when needed for dispatch. This owner correction supersedes the earlier requirement for both role heartbeat reports to always list it. Native timer text remains the canonical entry only.

The user report shows:
- Authorized Elite and Expert preset IDs (`runtime/tier`), counts and applicable grant lifetime.
- Currently occupied seats and their linked tasks.
- Idle, available capacity within each effective grant; held/unavailable/unknown shown separately.

Count a shared seat group once across its permitted tiers. Idle but unreclaimed/reserved sessions are not automatically available. Actual service and resource constraints still apply. Authorized capacity is derived from the individual/shared grants; no separate aggregate concurrency cap is stored. Host and Sideagent roles do not consume worker seats. Show no Expert authorization as none, without implying a grant.

Derive the report from existing current authorization and verified occupancy/task links. Do not create a second writable seat table, copy occupancy into Delegator JSON, retain historical seat rows, or inject complete model profiles. Reuse the existing Host dispatch view when needed; no new mandatory Host reading or reporting cycle.

Acceptance: the generated Delegator reporting guidance and its user-facing current view expose the summary with correct shared counts, task links and available/held/unknown distinctions. Reuse applicable existing checks. Host access remains need-driven. No new permission, registry, timer or separate QA phase.

### Owner correction: seat counts are the authorization capacity (2026-10-06)

The authorization JSON records which runtime/tier choices or shared groups are granted and how many seats each has. Do not offer an independently writable aggregate concurrency cap such as `elite_cap`, `total_cap`, or an equivalent renamed field. This supersedes earlier language retaining an optional extra aggregate cap.

Compute available capacity from effective individual/shared grant counts and current occupancy. Shared tiers refer to one shared count, not separate additive grants. Derived totals may be shown to the user but are not another stored authorization value. Preserve model-switch scope, grant lifetime and applicable owner restrictions; keep service/quota/fault facts in their existing proper current-state locations, not an invented concurrency grant limit.

Update the existing admission and role/report projections to consume this same authority. Migration must remove obsolete standalone aggregate limits without changing individual/shared grants or interrupting active work; if legacy total-limit intent conflicts with grant counts, make that specific ambiguity actionable rather than silently inventing authority. For this run the owner explicitly revoked the old cap4: current individual/shared grants authorize six possible Elite worker seats.

Use existing affected checks to prove all granted seats can be used, shared counts are respected and excess per-grant admission remains refused. Do not substitute a huge numeric cap, another override list or a free-text capacity policy.

### Owner correction: minimal current facts and owner requirements only (2026-10-06)

The owner requires the two routinely read JSONs to allow only concise CURRENT information and effective owner requirements. This is a field/source/lifecycle design constraint, not a word blacklist or an instruction to shorten arbitrary prose. Ordinary project notes and original evidence outside these routinely injected surfaces retain their existing scope.

Personal source review found seven concrete groups to consolidate in this issue:

1. Remove independently writable aggregate concurrency limits, as already specified above. Capacity comes from individual/shared seat grants.
2. Keep model-switch authorization in one canonical grant/group location. Do not independently maintain both per-grant `model_switch` and a second `model_switches` list. Preserve the exact owner-approved choices and switching permission; a list of permitted tiers alone must not invent permission to switch a running seat.
3. Derive eligible/capability preset lists from current grants, the declared default Worker pool, exclusions, scoped holds and actual availability evidence. `capability_summary.presets` must not be a second manually maintained authority or a shortcut that bypasses those sources. Preserve unknown availability honestly.
4. Derive catalog-owned Class definitions, preset Class, profile and default model/effort from the existing version-matched catalog/templates. They remain visible in the appropriate Host view/candidate tool and user report, but are not separately agent-authored routine state. Retain explicit owner overrides as overrides, not copied defaults.
5. A shared grant has one authoritative count and one set of permitted choices/restrictions. Repeated tier rows must not each own a competing copy of the group count. Reuse the existing grouped owner grant representation and generate any compatibility rows mechanically. Do not add another group registry or lose per-choice restrictions.
6. Revoked/expired/completed entries are not authorization history to retain in current JSON. Remove settled entries. A still-effective exclusion of a default-authorized Worker preset remains a current exclusion; a revoked seat still requiring exact stop/handoff retains that CURRENT recovery duty until resolved. Do not erase those duties or silently restore default-pool authorization. A paused/on-hold grant remains authorized but unavailable, with its current reason and reopening route. No duplicate pause state in several independently writable collections.
7. Keep one concise current objective and original source pointers. Do not append issue-by-issue adoption history, earlier decisions, copied Skill rules or completed relay narratives into `project.goal`, `rules`, `requirements_source`, `watch` or equivalent fields. Task details stay with their current task/forge source. Resolved relays and exceptions leave routine state; history remains in the existing original evidence/Git/forge/Runner locations.

Owner requirements: project-specific owner requirements stay in the existing user section of AGENTS.md; current operating settings and grants use their existing typed configuration fields. Keep only a source reference in routine views when the source owns the full text. Do not create a second requirements narrative or let an agent invent requirements. Reflect a new owner correction by replacing superseded current content while preserving unfulfilled duties.

For each field retained, identify its authoritative writer/source and the CURRENT decision, delivery, recovery or consistency need it serves. Computable totals/occupancy/candidates are tool outputs, not independent agent-maintained records. Keep necessary exact identities, concurrency revisions, pending-delivery/maintenance sequence and scoped recovery checkpoints: these cannot safely be reconstructed from a count or current text. A tool-generated compatibility body/cache can remain where an actual consumer requires it; it must be regenerated from the same source and never become a second writable authority. Authorization relay/adoption across Delegator and Host must retain its real ownership boundary.

Apply this through the existing shared field contract, writers, consumer projections and migration. Do not merely hide duplicate stored fields in the user report. Reuse current checks to show a grant/count/switch/exclusion change updates every derived view, resolved records disappear without losing active duties, and old readers cannot silently expand authorization. Keep mixed-version limitations and actionable migration explicit. No new schema framework, state store, periodic full audit or blanket live-file rewrite is authorized by this correction. Preserve the active sole writer and in-flight work.

## QA and acceptance

Use existing contract tests plus targeted new cases and a bounded real Host/Sideagent run. No independent second QA framework. The outer Delegator personally reviews the integrated result with Opus Extra High before completion.

Required evidence:

- Unknown keys and invalid typed writes at nested levels are refused without partial mutation; direct unknown JSON/body edits do not enter updated routine projections. Valid unrelated work continues.
- Shared field contract covers all internal writers and all three role readers; tool-guided recovery can continue after refusals.
- Repeated cycles retain active duties, current owner intent and unresolved decisions while removing resolved warning/history duplication. No automatic semantic deletion of arbitrary text.
- Consumer cases above: sourced stage-warning resolution; closed versus genuinely pending task; exact Devin hold scope; two batches with first dispatch live; pending/delivered/adopted relay; missing/inactive Sideagent distinction.
- Correct Class/capability exposure remains present and grant-aware. No model selection or quota authorization changes.
- Read actual files written/migrated by the new tool with v0.9.0 `execute` both via authorization-file and separate state-file paths: same holds, pauses and live task-seat facts. Named receipt if historical fixture unavailable; no silent skip.
- Interrupted/repeated migration, concurrent Host/node updates, malformed holds, older holder/tool, unavailable timer readback and urgent owner stop retain useful recovery without new blanket gates.
- No new durable snapshot/history files during repeated successful or interrupted migration; JSON cleanup retains pending duties and only necessary fixed deduplication metadata; completed evidence is retrievable at its existing Git path/commit. Do not force-add ignored runtime state.
- Required checks for affected surfaces and truthful limitations. New holder behavior tested through the existing ACP start/send/observe/return/stop path; do not substitute only JSON-shape tests for actual injection evidence.

## Coordination and exclusions

#258 already owns the baseline Unreleased assertion; do not duplicate it. Sparse-checkout/sink behavior and stale KW sink receipt fields are separate recovery findings, not reasons to redesign this state contract.

Opus also found that current `shared_seat` admission treats every named group as capacity one, while this project's owner granted two shared Droid seats. Preserve the owner's two-seat grant. Reproduce and record that separate defect before selecting an admission fix; do not silently reinterpret the grant or bury that change inside record validation.

Local design references (supporting evidence, not required to understand this issue):
- `/tmp/kpr-record-contract-design-20261005.md` revision 2, NOT independently accepted.
- `/tmp/kpr-record-contract-addendum-20261005.md`, Opus consensus corrections; source analysis, not executed test proof.
- `/tmp/kpr-record-contract-r2-review-20261005.md`, outer review.
- `/tmp/kpr-consumer-record-findings-20261005.md`, consumer observations.

Preserve applicable repository/Workflow lifecycle and protected untracked files. Implement via the existing single Host; do not modify VRPAI/VRPCAD while using them as read-only observational evidence. Their migration/installation requires separate authorization.
